from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.setup_layout("Hook & The Prerequisite: Light's Speed in Vacuum",

                           "Light travels at constant speed in a vacuum.",

        # --- Pre-calculate elements ---
        water_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/water.svg")

        straw = Line(start=UP*1.5, end=DOWN*1.5, color=ORANGE, stroke_width=6)
        straw_in_water = VGroup(water_surface, straw, water_icon)
        self.place_in_area(straw_in_water, 'B4', 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)

        self.place_at_grid(light_beam, 'D3', scale_factor=0.7)

        speed_text = MathTex(r"c = 3 \times 10^8 \, m/s", color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(speed_text, 'E4', scale_factor=0.75)
        
        # Glass boundary
        boundary = VGroup(glass_icon)

        # --- Animations ---
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(Create(straw_in_water), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(FadeOut(straw_in_water), Create(light_beam), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Write(speed_text), Create(boundary), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Snell’s Law: The Geometric Rule", ["Snell's Law predicts how light bends.", "Wavefronts hit the medium at an angle.", "Slowing down causes the wavefront to pivot."])
        
        # Load assets
        laser = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/laser.svg")
        glass = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/glass.svg")
        
        # Create objects
        boundary = Line(start=np.array([-1, 0, 0]), end=np.array([1, 0, 0]), color=WHITE)
        normal = DashedLine(start=np.array([0, 1, 0]), end=np.array([0, -1, 0]), color="#808080")
        
        # Position objects using feedback constraints
        # Line 27: Boundary at B3-B4
        self.place_in_area(boundary, 'B3', 'B4', scale_factor=0.8)
        # Line 27: Normal at B5
        self.place_at_grid(normal, 'B5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        incident_ray = Arrow(start=np.array([-0.5, 0.5, 0]), end=np.array([0, 0, 0]), color="#FFFFFF", buff=0)
        refracted_ray = Arrow(start=np.array([0, 0, 0]), end=np.array([0.5, -0.5, 0]), color="#FFCC00", buff=0)
        
        # Formula
        formula = MathTex(r"n_1 \sin(\theta_1) = n_2 \sin(\theta_2)", color=WHITE)
        # Line 28: Formula at D3-E5
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'D3', 'E5', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Asset integration
        self.place_at_grid(laser, 'A4', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(glass, 'C4', scale_factor=0.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(incident_ray), Create(boundary), Create(normal), FadeIn(laser), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Create(refracted_ray), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(glass), Write(formula), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFCC00")

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Mathematical Visualization", [
            "Snell's Law is n1 sin theta1 equals n2 sin theta2.",
            "The beam bends toward or away from normal.",
            "Angles change in real-time as beam rotates."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Graph sin(theta 1) versus sin(theta 2) + prism asset
        prism = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/prism.svg", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(prism, "A3", scale_factor=0.3)
        self.add(prism)
        
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 1, 0.2], y_range=[0, 1, 0.2], axis_config={"include_numbers": False}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'C2', 'E4', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.add(axes)
        
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: x, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.play(Create(curve), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight slope as n1/n2 + protractor asset
        protractor = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/protractor.svg", color="#FF5500")
        self.place_at_grid(protractor, "A5", scale_factor=0.3)
        self.add(protractor)
        
        slope_label = MathTex("n_1/n_2", color="#FF5500").scale(0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(slope_label, 'D5', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Write(slope_label), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF5500")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Rotating beam + laser asset
        laser = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/laser.svg", color="#808080")
        self.place_at_grid(laser, "F2", scale_factor=0.3)
        self.add(laser)
        
        plane = NumberPlane(x_range=[-1, 1], y_range=[-1, 1], axis_config={"include_numbers": False}).scale(0.4)
        self.place_at_grid(plane, 'B4', scale_factor=0.7)
        angle = ValueTracker(PI/4)
        
        # Persistent mobject for the beam, updated via updater
        beam = Line(ORIGIN, 1.0 * RIGHT, color="#808080")
        beam.move_to(plane.get_center())
        beam.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_angle(angle.get_value()))
        self.add(beam)
        
        self.play(Create(plane), run_time=1)
        self.play(angle.animate.set_value(PI/6), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#808080")
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: The Physics of Refraction: Why Light Bends

sections.title: Hook & The Prerequisite: Light's Speed in Vacuum
sections.content: Start with a 30-second visual hook showing a 'broken' straw in a glass of water. Briefly recap that light travels at a constant speed (c) in a vacuum, which serves as our baseline reference.
sections.example: An archerfish hunting: It must account for the shift in perceived position to hit its prey through the water-air interface.

sections.title: Defining Refractive Index (n)
sections.content: Introduce the refractive index as a measure of 'optical density.' Use a graphical representation: A runner (light) moving on a track (vacuum) vs. moving through deep sand (a dense medium). The formula n = c / v is displayed as a simple ratio.
sections.example: Comparing light passing through air (n≈1) vs. diamond (n≈2.42), showing the corresponding 'speed limit' reduction in the material.

sections.title: Snell’s Law: The Geometric Rule
sections.content: Visualize the bending process. Use a 2D animation of a wavefront (represented by parallel lines) hitting a boundary at an angle. As one side hits the medium first and slows down, the entire 'wavefront' pivots.
sections.example: A marching band turning a corner: When the soldiers on the inside slow down, the whole line automatically pivots toward the slower medium.

sections.title: Mathematical Visualization
sections.content: Present Snell's Law (n1 * sin(θ1) = n2 * sin(θ2)). Instead of just text, use an interactive-style overlay showing the angles θ1 and θ2 changing in real-time as the light beam rotates toward or away from the 'normal' line.
sections.example: A laser pointer shining from air into a glass prism, showing the relationship between the incident angle and the refracted angle on a coordinate grid.

sections.title: Real-World Application & Summary
sections.content: Conclude by connecting the theory to human vision and technology. Summarize that refraction is the basis for all lens-based devices.
sections.example: The human eye: How the cornea and lens refract incoming light to focus a sharp image onto the retina, much like a camera lens focusing light onto a sensor.
